This week, several notable auctions have garnered attention for their unique items and charitable causes. Here's a summary of the latest news:

**Unabomber Memorabilia Auction**

The U.S. Marshal's office is currently holding an online auction of the personal effects of Ted Kaczynski, also known as the Unabomber. The auction, which ends on June 2, aims to raise $15 million to pay off a restitution order to his victims and their families. Items up for bid include Kaczynski's 35,000-word handwritten manifesto, which has a current bid of $17,525, and his iconic hoodie, which has reached $20,025. Other items, such as his Smith-Corona typewriter and hand-bowed wood saw, have attracted less attention. Art historian Elyse Luray believes that the auction has some collectibility, but crime memorabilia collector Scott Michaels thinks that the items are more valuable for their historical significance than their monetary worth.

**Celebrity Luggage Auction**

Kellan Lutz, star of the Twilight series, is teaming up with JetBlue and DoSomething.org to auction off his luggage for a good cause. The celebrity baggage auction, which is being held on eBay, aims to raise funds for youth groups across the country. Lutz's contribution includes his travel items, and he hopes that his bag will help raise serious funds for the charity. The first round of items auctioned off raised over $15,000, and the second round, which includes Lutz's bags and items from Taylor Swift and Jessica Simpson, is currently underway.

**Rare Film Reel Sells for Six-Figure Sum**

A rare film reel, Charlie Chaplin in Zepped, has been sold to collector Morace Park for a six-figure sum. The film, which is the only known surviving copy, shows Chaplin bringing down a German Zeppelin during a London raid in 1917. The seven-minute long reel is thought to contain some of the earliest known animation and was made as a morale-boosting film for British troops during World War One. Park bought the film reel in 2009, but it is now set to command a significant price due to its rarity and historical significance.
